text:
Maria: Heads-up — I'm prototyping an nsys/perfetto ingestion runner for CI to auto-capture perf traces for our serving runtime. Plan: run short synthetic workloads (kv-cache hot/cold, batch-size sweep, jittered seq lengths), tag traces with marker events, and push artifacts to s3 for the diff dashboard. Will push a PoC to infra branch later today.

Raj: Nice. Two quick asks: 1) keep artifact sizes manageable, 2) make deep captures conditional on regression. Full nsys every night will kill storage.

Oliver: +1. Suggest two capture modes: `summary` (CUPTI counters + condensed kernel timeline) and `deep` (full nsys/trace). Default to `summary` nightly, trigger `deep` if summary shows >2% token-latency regression or a new hotspot.

Zane: How do we avoid noisy KV-cache churn causing false positives? We need controlled workloads that exercise cold/hot cache explicitly and reproducible seeds. Also need stable kernel naming for dashboard diffs.

Maria: Good point. My runner will include explicit phases: warmup (populate KV), cold-lookup sweep, mixed batch sweep, and a randomized short-run to exercise different kernel paths. We'll attach a small metadata JSON with kernel selection logs so diffs can map to runtime decisions.

Raj: For artifact size reduction: strip whole-host memory dumps, compress with zstd, and keep only kernel timestamps + samples above a threshold. Example command for a summary capture: `nsys profile --sample=cupti,osrt --trace=cuda,cupti --duration=12s -o out_summary`. For deep: `nsys profile -o out_deep --capture-range=cpu:nsys_marker_start,nsys_marker_end`.

Oliver: Also add perfetto export for timeline visualizations (`perfetto --import out_deep.qdpack --run_ui`). Marker events inserted in code will make it easy to align request boundaries. We should add an invariant in the runner that ensures markers exist or fail the job.

perf-ci-bot: New artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/traces/2026-06-11/1768456789_summary.tar.zst (size ~320MB).

Zane: 320MB still high but manageable. What's retention policy? We should keep summaries for 90 days and deep traces for 30 days unless referenced by a regression ticket. Archive deep traces to cold storage automatically.

Maria: Agreed. I'll set lifecycle rules in infra: summary -> 90d S3 standard, deep -> 30d then Glacier. Also will add an option to scrub any env vars or keys before uploading.

Raj: Nice. One more: batching heuristics testing — include a sweep over batch sizes [1,4,8,16] and variable seq-len distributions to surface kernel selection differences. Log the runtime's kernel-selection decision alongside the trace so the diff dashboard can attribute regressions to a changed kernel selector.

Oliver: On the diff dashboard side, we need stable metric keys: p50/p95 token latency, kernel occupancy %, and a hashed signature of kernel list + compiled flags. That signature can be used to group identical builds.

Maria: I'll add `--mode=summary|deep`, `--test=<kv_warm_cold|batch_sweep>`, and `--out=...` flags to the runner. Example invocation: `./tools/perf-ci-runner --mode=summary --test=kv_warm_cold --out=/tmp/artifacts/1768456789_summary.tar.zst`. Also will include small README and the infra job YAML.

Raj: Let's roll this out behind an opt-in 2-week trial on a subset of nightly workers, then expand. Make sure to add a size quota per job in CI to avoid runaway costs.

Zane: And add an automated check that the runner strips any PII or client keys; maybe run a scanner before upload.

Maria: Will do. I'll open a PR with the runner + infra job + dashboard mapping. ETA: draft PR by EOD tomorrow.

Oliver: Great. Thanks — looking forward to seeing kernel timelines in the dashboard.

perf-ci-bot: Perf CI job started: build/1768456789 -> runner summary -> artifact saved.

Maria: FYI I'll follow up with a tiny PoC trace excerpt in the PR so the dashboard mapping team can test ingestion.
